course_title: Networking Foundations: From Packet to Production
lesson_title: How Data Moves Through a Network
objective: Explain encapsulation and the roles of links, switches, routers, and applications.
explanation: Data moves as application data wrapped into transport segments, network packets, and link frames. Each device makes a decision at its own layer.
practice: Draw the path of a browser request across two networks. Label MAC addresses, IP addresses, ports, and where each value changes.
expected_outcome: Submit the annotated path and identify the first device that can route the packet.

course_title: Networking Foundations: From Packet to Production
objective: Create an isolated lab where network failures can be reproduced without affecting real users.
explanation: A useful lab has known endpoints, an explicit topology, observable traffic, and a reset path. Isolation matters more than size.
practice: Build two client nodes and one service using containers or virtual machines. Record addresses and prove baseline reachability.
expected_outcome: Provide the topology, address plan, and successful connectivity checks before introducing a fault.

course_title: Networking Foundations: From Packet to Production
objective: Predict how a switch learns and forwards frames inside and across VLAN boundaries.
explanation: Switches learn source MAC addresses per VLAN and forward by destination MAC. VLANs create separate broadcast domains.
practice: Observe ARP and MAC learning, then separate two hosts into different VLANs and explain why routing becomes necessary.
expected_outcome: Capture the ARP exchange and a MAC table snapshot with a short explanation of the forwarding decision.

course_title: Networking Foundations: From Packet to Production
objective: Turn a host requirement into a correct subnet and usable address range.
explanation: A prefix divides network bits from host bits. Subnet design balances address capacity, broadcast boundaries, and future growth.
practice: Calculate /24, /26, and /28 ranges, then create an address plan for three teams without overlap.
expected_outcome: Provide network, broadcast, first and last usable addresses plus a check using a subnet tool.

course_title: Networking Foundations: From Packet to Production
objective: Explain how addressing, name resolution, and routing cooperate before an application can connect.
explanation: DHCP supplies configuration, DNS maps names to addresses, and routers select a next hop. A failure in any stage can look like an application outage.
practice: Trace a new client from DHCP lease through DNS resolution to a routed service request and deliberately break one stage.
expected_outcome: Submit the lease, resolver result, route decision, and the observed symptom of the injected failure.

course_title: Networking Foundations: From Packet to Production
objective: Diagnose network faults from evidence instead of changing multiple settings at once.
explanation: Start at scope and symptoms, form one hypothesis, test the lowest relevant layer, and move upward only when evidence supports it.
practice: Repair three faults: link unavailable, wrong gateway, and failed DNS. Use one command or capture to prove each root cause.
expected_outcome: Provide a timeline of hypothesis, test, result, fix, and independent verification for every fault.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
objective: Separate provider responsibilities from the controls a workload owner must implement.
explanation: Responsibility changes across infrastructure, managed platforms, and software services, but ownership of data and access never disappears.
practice: Classify ten operational tasks across EC2, RDS, and a managed object store, then mark the accountable party.
expected_outcome: Submit the responsibility matrix and explain two controls that remain yours in every service model.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
lesson_title: Regions, Availability Zones and Failure Boundaries
objective: Choose a deployment boundary that matches recovery and latency needs.
explanation: Regions isolate geography; availability zones isolate infrastructure failure. Resilience comes from independent copies and tested recovery paths.
practice: Design a service across two availability zones and document what happens when one zone is unavailable.
expected_outcome: Provide the diagram, recovery objective, dependency list, and a probe that proves the surviving path works.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
objective: Design identities and permissions that grant only the actions a role needs.
explanation: Authentication proves identity; authorization limits actions. Short-lived role credentials reduce the impact of leaked secrets.
practice: Replace an administrator-style policy with task-specific permissions for an application and an operator.
expected_outcome: Submit the policy rationale plus one allowed and one denied action from a policy simulation or sandbox test.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
lesson_title: VPC Design: Public and Private Paths
objective: Design subnets, routes, and controls for internet-facing and internal components.
explanation: A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway; workload exposure also depends on addresses and security controls. Private workloads use explicit egress paths.
practice: Create a two-AZ address plan with public ingress and private application and data tiers.
expected_outcome: Provide CIDR calculations, route intent, and a flow explanation from user to database and back.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
objective: Connect scaling and load balancing decisions to measurable health signals.
explanation: A load balancer distributes only to healthy targets; scaling changes capacity from observed demand while deployment strategy limits blast radius.
practice: Define health, scaling, and deployment rules for a stateless API with two failure scenarios.
expected_outcome: Submit thresholds, expected routing behavior, and the probe used to confirm healthy service.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
objective: Choose storage and database services from access pattern, consistency, durability, and recovery needs.
explanation: Object, block, file, relational, and key-value systems optimize different constraints. Recovery design includes backup, restore, and verification.
practice: Compare two data designs for user uploads and transactional metadata, then rehearse a restore in a sandbox.
expected_outcome: Provide the decision table, recovery objective, restore result, and integrity check.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
objective: Define signals that reveal user impact while keeping resource cost visible.
explanation: Metrics show trends, logs explain events, and traces connect distributed work. Cost is another operational signal tied to usage and ownership.
practice: Create a small dashboard and budget plan for latency, errors, saturation, and daily spend.
expected_outcome: Submit alert thresholds, owner, runbook link, and one test alert with its cost assumption.

course_title: AWS Cloud Foundations and Well-Architected Thinking
objective: Turn architecture risks into prioritized, testable improvements.
explanation: A review is a conversation about evidence and trade-offs across operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, cost, and sustainability.
practice: Review the weekly workload, rank three risks by likelihood and impact, and define one measurable remediation for each.
expected_outcome: Provide the risk register, chosen priorities, owners, and acceptance evidence for the highest-risk improvement.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
objective: Explain the difference between an immutable image and a running container.
explanation: An image is a layered filesystem plus metadata; a container adds a writable layer and an isolated process. Data that must survive belongs outside that writable layer.
practice: Inspect an image history, run two containers from it, change one container, and compare their state.
expected_outcome: Submit image digest, layer summary, process list, and proof that the second container remains unchanged.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
objective: Build a reproducible image with a small attack surface and effective cache use.
explanation: Dockerfile order shapes build cache reuse. Multi-stage builds separate compilation tools from the runtime image.
practice: Create a multi-stage build, add a precise ignore file, pin the base version, and compare image size and rebuild time.
expected_outcome: Provide the Dockerfile, image digest, size comparison, and cached build output.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
objective: Choose the correct persistence and communication mechanism for a multi-container app.
explanation: Named volumes outlive containers; bind mounts expose host files. User-defined networks provide scoped DNS-based service discovery.
practice: Connect an application to a database by service name, persist its data, remove the containers, and recreate them.
expected_outcome: Submit network inspection, volume inspection, and proof that data survives container recreation.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
objective: Describe a complete local stack as versioned configuration.
explanation: Compose defines services, networks, volumes, configuration, dependencies, and health, but startup order alone does not guarantee readiness.
practice: Build an app, database, and worker stack with health checks and environment defaults that contain no secrets.
expected_outcome: Provide the resolved Compose config, healthy service list, and one-command setup and teardown instructions.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
lesson_title: Health Checks, Signals and Graceful Shutdown
objective: Make container lifecycle behavior observable and safe during replacement.
explanation: PID 1 must receive signals and stop work cleanly. Readiness describes ability to serve; liveness describes whether recovery is required.
practice: Add a health check and graceful termination handler, then stop the container during an active request.
expected_outcome: Submit timestamps showing signal receipt, request completion or safe cancellation, and exit code.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
lesson_title: Run as Non-root and Scan the Supply Chain
objective: Reduce privileges and identify known risk before publishing an image.
explanation: A secure container combines trusted inputs, minimal contents, non-root runtime, controlled secrets, and continuous vulnerability review.
practice: Switch the runtime user, remove build tools, scan the image, and document one accepted or remediated finding.
expected_outcome: Provide user identity inside the container, scan summary, base image source, and remediation decision.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
objective: Publish and identify an exact image without relying on a mutable tag.
explanation: Tags are convenient pointers; digests identify immutable content. Promotion should move a verified artifact between environments without rebuilding it.
practice: Tag a release, record its digest, and verify the pulled artifact matches what passed tests.
expected_outcome: Submit registry reference, digest comparison, and the rule used to prevent accidental latest-tag deployment.

course_title: Docker Engineering: Containers to Production
objective: Design a delivery gate and diagnose common runtime failures from evidence.
explanation: A reliable pipeline builds once, tests the artifact, scans it, publishes by digest, and deploys with health verification and rollback criteria.
practice: Draft a pipeline and debug one crash loop, one port mismatch, and one permission failure.
expected_outcome: Provide the pipeline stages and, for each fault, the log or inspection evidence, fix, and independent health check.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
lesson_title: Define the Task, User and Success Metric
objective: Translate a product need into a measurable machine-learning task and explicit decision boundary.
explanation: A useful model starts with who acts on the output, what decision changes, the cost of errors, and a baseline that can be beaten.
practice: Write a one-page task brief with user, input, output, latency, false-positive and false-negative costs, and acceptance metric.
expected_outcome: Submit the task brief and explain why the chosen metric represents user value better than raw accuracy.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
lesson_title: Build a Data Contract and Prevent Leakage
objective: Define trustworthy inputs and create train, validation, and test splits that reflect deployment.
explanation: A data contract states schema, provenance, consent, quality, and freshness. Leakage occurs when training uses information unavailable at prediction time.
practice: Audit a sample dataset, define validation rules, and split it by the unit and time boundary used in production.
expected_outcome: Provide schema checks, split logic, class distribution, and one leakage risk you removed.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
objective: Create the simplest credible model and record enough context to reproduce it.
explanation: A baseline tests whether the problem and data contain useful signal. Reproducibility requires versioned code, data reference, configuration, and random seed.
practice: Train a simple baseline, compare it with a rule-based guess, and record the experiment inputs and result.
expected_outcome: Submit the run configuration, dataset version, metric table, and exact command that reproduces the result.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
lesson_title: Use Error Analysis to Improve the System
objective: Find meaningful failure groups instead of tuning only an aggregate score.
explanation: Aggregate metrics hide uneven performance. Error slices connect model behavior to data quality, product rules, and affected users.
practice: Review false positives and false negatives, group them by cause, and choose one change based on impact and frequency.
expected_outcome: Provide a confusion matrix, three error slices, representative sanitized examples, and the next experiment hypothesis.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
objective: Expose model inference through a bounded, versioned contract with predictable failure behavior.
explanation: The service contract owns input validation, preprocessing parity, timeouts, output schema, and traceable model version.
practice: Create an endpoint specification with valid, invalid, and timeout cases plus a health endpoint separate from inference.
expected_outcome: Submit request and response examples, error contract, latency target, and model-version field.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
lesson_title: Test and Version the Whole Pipeline
objective: Catch divergence across data preparation, model artifact, API behavior, and deployment.
explanation: Unit tests protect transforms, contract tests protect interfaces, and golden examples protect expected behavior. Versioning ties an output to its inputs.
practice: Add transform tests, API contract tests, and five golden examples, then replay them against a packaged artifact.
expected_outcome: Provide test results, model and data versions, artifact checksum, and the golden-example comparison.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
lesson_title: Monitor Quality, Drift and Service Health
objective: Detect when an AI service becomes unavailable, slow, or less trustworthy.
explanation: Operational signals cover latency and errors; data signals cover schema and drift; quality signals require delayed labels or reviewed samples.
practice: Define a dashboard and response plan for latency, error rate, input drift, prediction distribution, and sampled quality.
expected_outcome: Submit thresholds, owner, investigation query, rollback rule, and a simulated alert result.

course_title: Applied AI Engineering: Data to Reliable Service
objective: Design safeguards proportional to data sensitivity and the impact of automated decisions.
explanation: Responsible operation combines data minimization, access controls, subgroup evaluation, transparent limitations, and a clear human escalation path.
practice: Create a risk register, compare performance across relevant slices, and design a review queue for uncertain or high-impact predictions.
expected_outcome: Provide the risk register, slice metrics, retention rule, review criteria, and one example where the human can override safely.
